fix.digest: Coda on later events, not recorded by Walker himself. On Friday 20 June 2014, in the centenary year of Ovonramwen's death, Walker's grandson Mark Walker handed the brass bird and bell that the captain had taken in 1897 to the Oba of Benin, with a copy of his grandfather's diary. Press reports of the day say the diary ran from his departure from Liverpool to his return and that the palace received the grandson as a friend of the city.

problem: Luschan died in 1924 but is shown 'recording' the 2022 handover. Must be an explicit editor's coda about the collection he built.

fix.headline: Coda, 2022: Germany hands back the first twenty
fix.digest: Coda on later events, long after Luschan's death in 1924. On 20 December 2022 Germany's foreign minister handed over the first twenty Benin objects in Abuja (Nigeria counted 22), after the two governments agreed that year to transfer ownership of Benin objects in German museums. Berlin, whose collection Luschan had built, signed over its 512 objects on 25 August 2022; about a third stay on loan in Berlin. Positions differ: the German government called it a step in facing its colonial past; Nigeria's culture minister thanked Germany; the British Museum says the British Museum Act 1963 bars it from giving up its collection.
fix.form: editor's coda (later event, from official statements and press reports)
fix.source_note: NPR, 21 Dec 2022; SMB Benin collection page (contract of 25 Aug 2022). Later event; not recorded by Luschan. The British Museum's position is as widely reported.
